content.text: : potent inhibitors of bone resorption; bind to hydroxyapatite crystals in bone & antagonize osteoclast activity; osteoclast activation, formation, & recruitment are inhibited, & life span is reduced; increase osteoblast proliferation & intestinal calcium absorption
: first line treatment/prevention of OP in most pts
: esophagitis, MSK sxs, hypocalcemia, GI (oral) – abdominal pain, dyspepsia, N/V, dysphagia, heartburn
: osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ), atypical femur fractures – limit tx to 3-5yrs in pts w/ low risk of fracture
: caution in pts w/ aspirin-sensitive asthma – can induce bronchoconstriction
•Estrogen Agonist: bone (↓ resorption), lipids, coagulation system
•Estrogen Antagonist: breast, uterus (↓ risk of breast cancer & endometrial cancer)
: treatment or prevention in postmenopausal women
: vasomotor sxs (hot flashes), GU atrophy, peripheral edema, arthralgia, leg cramps/muscle spasms, flu sxs, infections
: stimulates osteoblast function, increases gastrointestinal calcium absorption, and increases renal tubular reabsorption of calcium
: used in pts w/ a high risk of fracture for up to 2yrs
: arthralgias, leg cramps, pain, nausea, dizziness/orthostasis
Avoid in pts at risk for osteosarcoma
: osteosarcoma – dependent on dose/duration of tx
: RANKL inhibitor – results in decreased bone resorption & increased bone mass & strength
: used for tx when there is a high risk of fracture in pts who cannot adhere to or tolerate oral bisphosphonates
: serious systemic/skin infections, dermatologic reactions (dermatitis, eczema, rashes), ONJ
: monoclonal antibody that inhibits sclerostin, with the net effects of increasing bone formation and decreasing bone resorption (lesser effect)
: OP treatment in postmenopausal women at high risk for fracture or failed/intolerant to other therapy
: potential risk of MI, stroke, & CV death

: functionally antagonizes the effects of parathyroid hormone; directly inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption; promotes the renal excretion of calcium, phosphate, sodium, magnesium, and potassium by decreasing tubular reabsorption; increases the jejunal secretion of water, sodium, potassium, and chloride

: last line therapy/not recommended – used for pts who cannot tolerate or fail alendronate or raloxifene therapy; only recommended as a tx option for women >5yr postmenopausal who cannot tolerate any other OP medication
: back pain, myalgia, nausea, dizziness, injection (flushing & injection site reactions)

: hypocalcemia (associated w/ tetany/seizures), increased risk of malignancy w/ long-term use, hypersensitivity to salmon-derived products, antibody formation, nasal spray (nasal ulcerations, epistaxis, rhinitis)
